Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> The category of universal homeomorphisms <MATH_0002> has
an initial object <MATH_0003>.
<STRUCT_0003> Given <MATH_0004> in the category of (1) the resulting morphism
<MATH_0005> is an isomorphism if and only if <MATH_0006> is
absolutely weakly normal.
<STRUCT_0004> The category of universal homeomorphisms <MATH_0007> which
induce ismomorphisms on residue fields has an initial object
<MATH_0008>.
<STRUCT_0005> Given <MATH_0009> in the category of (3) the resulting morphism
<MATH_0010> is an isomorphism if and only if <MATH_0011> is seminormal.
<STRUCT_0006>
For any morphism <MATH_0012> of schemes there are unique morphisms
<MATH_0013> and <MATH_0014>
compatible with <MATH_0015>.

We will prove (1) and (2) and omit the proof of (3) and (4).
Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of schemes. If (1) holds for <MATH_0002>
and <MATH_0003>, then <MATH_0004> is a universal homeomorphism
and hence we get a unique morphism <MATH_0005>
over <MATH_0006> by the universal property of <MATH_0007>. Composed with the
projection <MATH_0008> we obtain <MATH_0009>.
If in addition (2) holds for <MATH_0010> and <MATH_0011> and <MATH_0012> is an open immersion, then
<MATH_0013> is absolutely weakly normal
(Lemma <REF_0001>) and we deduce that
<MATH_0014> is an isomorphism.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Recall that any universal homeomorphism is affine, see
Lemma <REF_0002>. Thus if <MATH_0015> is affine
then (1) and (2) follow immediately from
Lemma <REF_0003>.
Let <MATH_0016> be a scheme and let <MATH_0017> be the set of affine opens
of <MATH_0018>. For each <MATH_0019> we obtain <MATH_0020>
and for <MATH_0021>, <MATH_0022> we obtain a canonical
isomorphism <MATH_0023> by the discussion
in the previous paragraph. Thus by relative glueing
(Constructions, Lemma <REF_0004>)
we obtain a morphism <MATH_0024> which restricts
to <MATH_0025> over <MATH_0026> compatibly with the <MATH_0027>.
Next, let <MATH_0028> be a universal homeomorphism.
Then <MATH_0029> is a universal homeomorphism for <MATH_0030>
and we obtain a unique morphism <MATH_0031> over <MATH_0032>.
These <MATH_0033> are compatible with the morphisms <MATH_0034>; details
omitted. Hence there is a unique morphism <MATH_0035>
over <MATH_0036> agreeing with <MATH_0037> over <MATH_0038>, see
Constructions, Remark <REF_0005>.
This proves (1) for <MATH_0039>. Part (2) follows because it holds affine locally.
